coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Handling evidence is method-specific. Ladan and colleagues collected breast tissue in their specified medium, cut 300 micrometre slices and assessed morphology, proliferation and apoptosis after three-day exposure. This is not a general transport or storage protocol for all screens. Growth-rate methods show why baseline counts and control division affect interpretation. Retain failures and exclusions; failed preparation is not clinical resistance. A laboratory concentration is not a safe human dose.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. coverageEvidence.excerpt: In statistics and machine learning, leakage is the use of information during training that would not be available at prediction time, which produces overly optimistic performance estimates (Wikipedia). Common cancer-data forms are normalising or selecting genes on the full cohort before splitting, duplicated patients across TCGA and cBioPortal studies, and benchmark contamination, where a foundation model's pretraining corpus contained the public test set (TCGA slides or profiles), so that its downstream score is partly recall.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Ladan's real study began with 41 consenting people: three did not undergo biopsy and eight biopsies lacked tumour cells, leaving 30 adequate tumour biopsies. Six assays failed the prespecified baseline-apoptosis criterion and one was lost to infection. Of 23 usable results, three people did not receive the chemotherapy, leaving 20 clinical comparisons. The main-text counts are used here; Table 2's footnote instead mentions two people not receiving chemotherapy. The reported interval for 15/20 agreement was 53 to 89 percent, and the pilot's prespecified target was at least 55 percent. Reaching that target supports further investigation, not a demonstration that using the assay to choose care improves outcomes.

points.heading: Try it
points.requirement: A virtual model predicts less RNA for growth genes after an unseen drug. A laboratory well also shows less metabolic signal. Has this established tumor-cell killing?

sourceRefs.exactPassage: A virtual model predicts less RNA for growth genes after an unseen drug. A laboratory well also shows less metabolic signal. Has this established tumor-cell killing?

points.entailment: Predicted RNA plus a lower metabolic signal cannot establish killing. The answer names the actual object, cell attribution, starting/control reference and direct death/recognition comparisons still needed.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Fictional example. A tumour-only culture repeatedly responds to Drug A. This does not test an immune-dependent Drug B or prove benefit because the cells came from a patient. Check the required immune interaction, actual intervention, endpoint and independent validation. Repeatability cannot repair a mismatch between question and model. A simpler model may isolate a mechanism, while another model is needed for an interaction absent from it. More components alone do not show better prediction.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Preserve the original prediction and version before measuring an independent outcome, compare against the original rule, then investigate agreement, discordance and failures before developing a revision and testing it on new reserved data. A prospective evaluation fixes its predictions before the corresponding outcomes; retrospective analysis examines material and outcomes already observed. Neither label alone establishes useful care. If the toy team changes v1 after inspecting three false positives, v2 is development and v1's matrix and ten no-results remain unchanged. The later breast-study exercise likewise imagines revising a rule after three sensitive dish calls matched intermediate MRI outcomes; those comparisons are not assumed truth labels. Reusing the same twenty cases evaluates fit to the information used for revision. A move from advanced-disease drug A to postoperative drug B changes intended use again, and improvement during several treatments cannot isolate which treatment helped.

points.heading: What is still uncertain
points.requirement: Published agreement studies are small and setting-specific: a breast-slice anthracycline assay matched MRI response in 15 of 20 evaluable patients but never called a tumor resistant ([Ladan 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/)). Those studies measure agreement, not whether choosing treatment by the model improves outcomes. A model may also omit a relevant population, change during establishment or use an exposure that does not translate to patients. Computation may fail in a new context. Even a strong clinical prediction may lack evidence that its use improves care. Keep those gaps beside the useful result.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The reported breast-study totals imply two sensitive dish calls with sensitive MRI, three sensitive dish calls with intermediate MRI, two intermediate dish calls with sensitive MRI and thirteen intermediate calls matching MRI. Thus 15/20 agree, including thirteen matches in the common intermediate category. Two of four MRI-sensitive tumours were called sensitive in the dish (50 percent), and two of five sensitive dish calls matched MRI sensitivity (40 percent). These are stated comparisons with an imperfect MRI outcome, not validated sensitivity or positive predictive value against known truth. FDA's March 2007 diagnostic-test guidance distinguishes agreement from accuracy when the comparator is not a reference standard. The study's sensitive category required more than 50 percent size reduction after four chemotherapy courses; it is not simply the standard RECIST partial-response category. Usable coverage is 23/30, about 77 percent; a matching clinical comparison was available for 15/30, or 50 percent, including failures and the untreated people in that denominator. Neither ratio measures postoperative benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Read each omitted compartment. A tumour-only dish lacks required immune interactions unless those populations are added and shown functional. A fresh slice may retain resident neighbours while losing blood flow and recruitment from circulation. A conventional PDX adds mouse circulation, exposure and metabolism without reproducing an intact human immune system. A computational prediction depends on its data, assumptions and benchmark. Human-derived tissue can be used in both dish and animal models; do not claim that ex vivo is the only setting using human tissue. A living specimen can lose cells, adapt or undergo selection after removal; retaining a structure is not retaining complete physiology. In-vitro preparations can isolate direct effects, compare doses and drugs and support repeats, while omitting perfused blood supply, host metabolism and the original population mix unless specifically reconstructed. Latin labels such as in glass, out of the living and in the living are mnemonics for setting, not quality grades.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Wensink's 2021 review included seventeen publications, five about colorectal cancer; seven used metastatic populations. Its pooled sensitivity was 81 percent and specificity 74 percent for the included response comparisons. The authors warned that these estimates were likely high because some studies lacked quantitative results needed for pooling and not all used a predefined index test; publication or outcome-reporting bias could not be excluded. The pooled establishment estimate was 68.0 percent at patient level and 68.5 percent at sample level, with heterogeneous studies and wide intervals. These are different quantities from response agreement and from clinical utility. The review also reports a 34-day median just to establish organoids from breast biopsies, distinct from a completed drug panel or an individual decision deadline.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The prospective single-arm SENSOR study enrolled 61 people with metastatic colorectal cancer: 54 were eligible, 31 organoids were generated, 25 cultures were screened against eight drugs and nineteen showed a substantial laboratory response. Six people received an organoid-selected treatment, three vistusertib and three capivasertib, with no objective clinical responses. That observation concerns this panel and selected population; it neither establishes benefit from using the assay nor proves that every organoid method is ineffective. Guillen and colleagues' breast-model report describes a complete response in one person with metastatic triple-negative disease after a model-nominated treatment. That case demonstrates feasibility, without a comparison estimating how often the strategy helps.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

points.entailment: Independent intended-use prediction and improved care are distinct evidence questions; a measured model response alone does not establish either.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility address different questions for a specified assay, specimen, population and intended use. MedlinePlus Genetics distinguishes detection of a genetic variant, its relationship to disease presence or risk, and whether the information helps diagnosis, treatment, management or prevention. Reliable measurement does not by itself establish clinical meaning, and an outcome association does not establish benefit from changing care. For a prediction model, reproducibility of fixed-input output, discrimination, calibrated probabilities and the consequences of model-guided decisions also require distinct evidence. These are related questions rather than a universal sequence that guarantees a useful test.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A trial defines primary, secondary and exploratory outcomes and how they are measured and analysed. The primary question informs design, sample size and testing; having a secondary endpoint does not by itself establish whether it was adequately powered or met a prespecified testing rule. Overall survival concerns death from any cause, while response, progression, symptoms and quality of life answer different questions. A composite endpoint combines specified events, so its definition and starting time matter. FDA's December 2018 nonbinding oncology-endpoint guidance distinguishes direct clinical benefit and context-dependent surrogate evidence; use in an approval does not make an endpoint interchangeable with survival in every setting.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: External evaluation applies an existing model to data outside its development and compares predictions with observed outcomes. The TRIPOD-Cluster explanation includes later-period data collected by the same investigators as well as data from another hospital, country or care setting. A different platform is not a universal requirement. Apparent performance uses the development data and can be optimistic. Internal validation with resampling can estimate optimism and performance for new people from the same source population; it is evidence about a different question, rather than no result. External evaluation quantifies performance and its uncertainty instead of conferring a universal pass or fail. Keep the locked method, population, outcome, follow-up and differences from development visible.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Positive predictive value is the proportion of positive test calls that meet a specified reference condition: true positives divided by true plus false positives. A positive result can be a true positive or a false positive; a false positive is a positive call in someone without that reference condition. Negative predictive value uses negative calls as its denominator. These differ from sensitivity and specificity, which start with reference-condition groups. The population base rate, reference standard, threshold and actual assay performance determine how the fractions should be interpreted.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A trial defines primary, secondary and exploratory outcomes and how they are measured and analysed. The primary question informs design, sample size and testing; having a secondary endpoint does not by itself establish whether it was adequately powered or met a prespecified testing rule. Overall survival concerns death from any cause, while response, progression, symptoms and quality of life answer different questions. A composite endpoint combines specified events, so its definition and starting time matter. coverageEvidence.excerpt: A surrogate is a measured outcome used in place of a direct clinical-benefit outcome, with evidence needed for that substitution in the intended setting. Two relationships must be separated: people with a favourable marker may have better outcomes, while treatments that improve that marker may or may not improve the outcome. The first is a prognostic association; the second concerns agreement between treatment effects across suitable randomised comparisons. A treatment can change another pathway, later disease or toxicity as well as the marker. Validation is specific to disease, treatment context and intended outcome. An early measure is not automatically validated, and regulatory acceptance in one programme does not transfer to another. “Validated” and “reasonably likely to predict benefit” carry different evidence claims. Even a pathology or imaging response does not capture every benefit and harm.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility address different questions for a specified assay, specimen, population and intended use. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Randomised outcome evidence must be assessed for the named assay and use rather than declared absent for all functional testing in solid tumours. Ranjan and colleagues reported a 2023 trial of ChemoID selection versus physician choice from the same chemotherapy list in 78 people with recurrent glioblastoma under the 2016 WHO definition. Enrolment stopped after a prespecified efficacy analysis; the intention-to-treat report gave median overall survival of twelve versus 7.5 months. Participants could provide viable tumour through surgery or biopsy, so the findings do not include every patient with recurrent glioblastoma. Cordgenics supported the assay resources, and two authors declared licensed intellectual-property interests. This is evidence for the studied strategy and population, without validating another assay, organoid system, postoperative breast decision or universal treatment rule.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Ladan's real study began with 41 consenting people: three did not undergo biopsy and eight biopsies lacked tumour cells, leaving 30 adequate tumour biopsies. Six assays failed the prespecified baseline-apoptosis criterion and one was lost to infection. Of 23 usable results, three people did not receive the chemotherapy, leaving 20 clinical comparisons. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Wensink's 2021 review included seventeen publications, five about colorectal cancer; seven used metastatic populations. Its pooled sensitivity was 81 percent and specificity 74 percent for the included response comparisons. coverageEvidence.excerpt: The prospective single-arm SENSOR study enrolled 61 people with metastatic colorectal cancer: 54 were eligible, 31 organoids were generated, 25 cultures were screened against eight drugs and nineteen showed a substantial laboratory response. points.heading: What is still uncertain
points.requirement: Published agreement studies are small and setting-specific: a breast-slice chemotherapy assay matched magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) response in 15 of 20 evaluable patients but never called a tumor resistant ([Ladan 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/)). A pooled review of 17 organoid studies found no randomized trial of organoid-guided treatment ([Wensink 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8042051/)). When colorectal patients were treated with organoid-selected drugs, none of 6 responded ([Ooft 2021](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33887686/)). Agreement is not proof that choosing treatment by the model improves outcomes. A model may also omit a relevant population, change during establishment or use an exposure that does not translate to patients. Computation may fail in a new context. Even a strong clinical prediction may lack evidence that its use improves care. Keep those gaps beside the useful result.

points.heading: preamble
points.requirement: **Before you start:** [Tumor heterogeneity](/wiki/education/concepts/cancer-biology/what-cancer-is/tumor-heterogeneity) explains why one sample can miss populations. An [organoid](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/functional-models/organoid) is a three-dimensional culture that self-organizes to reproduce selected tissue features. A [virtual cell model](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/computational-analysis/virtual-cell-model) computes selected properties or responses.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: **Before you start:** [Tumor heterogeneity](/wiki/education/concepts/cancer-biology/what-cancer-is/tumor-heterogeneity) explains why one sample can miss populations. An [organoid](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/functional-models/organoid) is a three-dimensional culture that self-organizes to reproduce selected tissue features. A [virtual cell model](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/computational-analysis/virtual-cell-model) computes selected properties or responses.

points.entailment: The prerequisite definitions are carried by the existing owners. A maintained line, organised culture and removed tissue do not designate interchangeable preparations or physiological settings.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Organoids self-organise selected structural or functional tissue features in three-dimensional culture. Patient-derived tumour organoids are one member of this broader family, rather than complete copies of a patient. Establishment and growth conditions select cells, and identity and relevant properties need checking against the source specimen. Conventional epithelial cultures often omit immune and supporting populations; specialised retention or added co-cultures require method-specific evidence. Their use for mechanism and drug-response experiments does not by itself establish clinical utility.

Output belongs to the chosen assay, such as counts, doubling time in hours or a death fraction with its denominator. Passage counts transfers, not a fixed number of divisions. Identity matching by human short tandem repeat profiling, mycoplasma testing and phenotype/growth checks address different questions. Establishment can fail or select subsets; no line-name cutoff predicts clinical sensitivity. Sources: https://www.atcc.org/resources/culture-guides/animal-cell-culture-guide ; https://www.atcc.org/-/media/resources/technical-documents/cell-line-authentication-test-recommendations.pdf?rev=7664fa886e5948018dfe198d484bb4eb Establishing a new line uses finite viable tissue and can select populations. A cell line need not be a monolayer. ATCC uses authentication broadly for verification of identity and freedom from contamination: short tandem repeat profiling compares repeated DNA stretches to test human-line identity, while mycoplasma and other contamination tests and relevant phenotype checks answer additional questions. Passing the identity test does not answer all of them.

points.entailment: Measured data can be computational input without living-cell exposure. Task, version, training context and new reserved evaluation remain attached; computation speed is not demonstrated clinical readiness.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 establishment and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to drug exposure, with tumour-type variation: 85 percent in colorectal specimens and 30 percent in breast specimens in that series. Ladan used three-day exposures and stated that results can be known in seven to fourteen days; this is a planned window, not an observed turnaround distribution. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Bioprinting controls deposition of biological materials to build an experimental construct. The printing plan, measured final geometry, viable cells and biological function are distinct evidence. Kolesky and colleagues printed cell-containing and removable inks, removed the temporary channel material, added endothelial lining and perfused engineered tissues. This tissue-engineering experiment did not demonstrate a complete human organ or cancer-treatment utility. Yi and colleagues reported a particular glioblastoma chip combining patient-derived tumour cells, endothelial cells and brain-derived matrix; its abstract supports that bounded example.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Chip devices can control selected cells, matrix, interfaces, transport or mechanical conditions. Their composition varies: channels do not automatically supply endothelium or immune cells. Huh's lung model separated alveolar and vascular compartments and imposed mechanical strain; Hassell studied lung cancer in defined engineered environments. Jenkins placed immune-containing organotypic spheroids in a collagen microfluidic compartment. These are capabilities of particular systems, not universal chip properties or validation for personal treatment selection.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The useful trade-off is preserved biology against time and repeatability. A characterised PDX supports growth under whole-animal dosing, usually on a months-long establishment clock. Expanded organoids support repeated direct tumour-cell experiments and panels, often over weeks; conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune cells, while Neal's specialised method retained them. A short-term fragment may preserve resident neighbours for a local-interaction question over days, but their function must be demonstrated. No preparation is universally more predictive because it is more complex. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2018.11.021 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4167608/

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

points.entailment: Original D0 and A/B/C project is wholly invented and kept distinct from the later named-drug scenario.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In a wholly fictional development project, D0 supplies one verified malignant preparation. Drug A asks about a direct repair perturbation: a tumour-only organoid supplies a viable-cell count after 48 hours, with division and death measured separately. coverageEvidence.excerpt: Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: In statistics and machine learning, leakage is the use of information during training that would not be available at prediction time, which produces overly optimistic performance estimates (Wikipedia). coverageEvidence.excerpt: Bioprinting controls deposition of biological materials to build an experimental construct. The printing plan, measured final geometry, viable cells and biological function are distinct evidence. Kolesky and colleagues printed cell-containing and removable inks, removed the temporary channel material, added endothelial lining and perfused engineered tissues. This tissue-engineering experiment did not demonstrate a complete human organ or cancer-treatment utility. Yi and colleagues reported a particular glioblastoma chip combining patient-derived tumour cells, endothelial cells and brain-derived matrix; its abstract supports that bounded example.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Chip devices can control selected cells, matrix, interfaces, transport or mechanical conditions. Their composition varies: channels do not automatically supply endothelium or immune cells. Huh's lung model separated alveolar and vascular compartments and imposed mechanical strain; Hassell studied lung cancer in defined engineered environments. These are capabilities of particular systems, not universal chip properties or validation for personal treatment selection.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Read each omitted compartment. A tumour-only dish lacks required immune interactions unless those populations are added and shown functional. A fresh slice may retain resident neighbours while losing blood flow and recruitment from circulation. A conventional PDX adds mouse circulation, exposure and metabolism without reproducing an intact human immune system. A computational prediction depends on its data, assumptions and benchmark. Human-derived tissue can be used in both dish and animal models; do not claim that ex vivo is the only setting using human tissue. A living specimen can lose cells, adapt or undergo selection after removal; retaining a structure is not retaining complete physiology. In-vitro preparations can isolate direct effects, compare doses and drugs and support repeats, while omitting perfused blood supply, host metabolism and the original population mix unless specifically reconstructed. Latin labels such as in glass, out of the living and in the living are mnemonics for setting, not quality grades.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Read a model study as a sequence of explicitly defined groups: people or specimens offered or submitted, preparations yielding a usable model, results compared with a clinical outcome, and results agreeing under the stated rule. Eligibility exclusions, absent tumour, laboratory failures, missing outcomes and people not receiving the treatment belong to different steps. State whether the unit is a person, specimen or treatment comparison; one person can contribute more than one. A percentage among compared cases cannot describe everyone originally offered testing, and an analysis exclusion is not automatically a failed culture. Keep the drug, cancer, treatment history, outcome, clock and assay version attached rather than ranking different studies as competing accuracy scores.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: The fictional locked rule yields twenty reports and ten no-results among thirty donors. Among reportable cases, six are true positive, three false positive, two false negative and nine true negative, using the exercise's assumed-correct reference labels. There are eight reference positives, twelve negatives, nine positive predictions and eleven negative predictions. Correct classifications are 15/20 (75 percent), sensitivity 6/8 (75 percent), specificity 9/12 (75 percent), and positive predictive value 6/9 (about 66.7 percent). Reportable coverage is 20/30 (about 66.7 percent); 15/30 (50 percent) received a correct reportable classification. The ten no-results keep blank predictions, unknown failure reasons and unspecified outcomes, rather than becoming negative or resistant cases. These truth-based toy metrics do not turn an imperfect real MRI comparator into truth or establish clinical utility.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Ladan's real study began with 41 consenting people: three did not undergo biopsy and eight biopsies lacked tumour cells, leaving 30 adequate tumour biopsies. Six assays failed the prespecified baseline-apoptosis criterion and one was lost to infection. Of 23 usable results, three people did not receive the chemotherapy, leaving 20 clinical comparisons. The main-text counts are used here; Table 2's footnote instead mentions two people not receiving chemotherapy. The reported interval for 15/20 agreement was 53 to 89 percent, and the pilot's prespecified target was at least 55 percent. Reaching that target supports further investigation, not a demonstration that using the assay to choose care improves outcomes.

The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: An evidence card records population, stage, treatment context and selection; specimen, handling, assay version and quality criteria; the reference condition or care comparator and its limitations; outcome and measurement time; the analysis plan, all tuning and independent evaluation; failed samples, dropout and missing outcomes; and sample size, intervals and remaining uncertainty. Neither alone establishes that the proposed clinical action helps. A headline metric also needs the consequences of false positive and false negative calls attached to the action. State whether a treatment-study denominator includes everyone assigned, only those treated or only those evaluable.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A trial defines primary, secondary and exploratory outcomes and how they are measured and analysed. The primary question informs design, sample size and testing; having a secondary endpoint does not by itself establish whether it was adequately powered or met a prespecified testing rule. Overall survival concerns death from any cause, while response, progression, symptoms and quality of life answer different questions. FDA's December 2018 nonbinding oncology-endpoint guidance distinguishes direct clinical benefit and context-dependent surrogate evidence; use in an approval does not make an endpoint interchangeable with survival in every setting.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: A surrogate is a measured outcome used in place of a direct clinical-benefit outcome, with evidence needed for that substitution in the intended setting. Two relationships must be separated: people with a favourable marker may have better outcomes, while treatments that improve that marker may or may not improve the outcome. The first is a prognostic association; the second concerns agreement between treatment effects across suitable randomised comparisons. A treatment can change another pathway, later disease or toxicity as well as the marker. Validation is specific to disease, treatment context and intended outcome. An early measure is not automatically validated, and regulatory acceptance in one programme does not transfer to another. “Validated” and “reasonably likely to predict benefit” carry different evidence claims. Even a pathology or imaging response does not capture every benefit and harm.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Positive predictive value is the proportion of positive test calls that meet a specified reference condition: true positives divided by true plus false positives. A positive result can be a true positive or a false positive; a false positive is a positive call in someone without that reference condition. Negative predictive value uses negative calls as its denominator. These differ from sensitivity and specificity, which start with reference-condition groups. The population base rate, reference standard, threshold and actual assay performance determine how the fractions should be interpreted.

coverageEvidence.excerpt: Primary preparation example. Ladan used 300 micrometre slices and three-day exposure in a defined anthracycline-based assay, measuring morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Diffusion into slices differs from vascular delivery; host metabolic activation, clearance, organ toxicity and new immune recruitment were not recreated. Preparation injury, poor viability, uneven diffusion, changing populations and non-tumour signal can invalidate interpretation. A failed culture is not evidence of clinical resistance. Contamination is another reason for assay failure; short-term response does not establish durable elimination, systemic safety or benefit.

Its study related protein abundance to shrinkage among people all receiving Drug A for advanced Cancer X. A favourable prognostic result does not itself justify omitting standard treatment.

FDA's March 2007 diagnostic-test guidance distinguishes agreement from accuracy when the comparator is not a reference standard. The study's sensitive category required more than 50 percent size reduction after four chemotherapy courses; it is not simply the standard RECIST partial-response category. Usable coverage is 23/30, about 77 percent; a matching clinical comparison was available for 15/30, or 50 percent, including failures and the untreated people in that denominator. Neither ratio measures postoperative benefit.

anchors.text: Conventional xenografts, epithelial organoids and short-term fragments make different trade-offs. Xenografts add a living host with mouse support and exposure. Organoids expand selected populations in supplied culture conditions. Fragments can retain local neighbours briefly without perfused circulation. This comparison describes preparations and decision windows; the existing model-context framework owns the broader question of intended-use validation.

anchors.text: A conventional xenograft implants viable tumour material into a host; an epithelial organoid grows selected cells in supplied matrix and medium; a fragment or slice retains a cut piece of local tissue. Ladan used 300 micrometre (0.3 millimetre) breast slices. None supplies complete human drug metabolism, healthy-organ toxicity or recruitment of new immune cells from human circulation, and every preparation can fail. Fixed archival tissue cannot supply the living input. Whether frozen material is usable must be shown for the particular protocol; Ladan's assay used fresh tissue.

anchors.text: Throughput and repetition depend on how material can be expanded. A xenograft can be passaged into further mice, but each drug comparison needs suitable animals and controls. An established organoid line can be expanded and passaged to compare a drug panel; Sachs reported retention of many source features during extended passaging, not unlimited fidelity. A cut piece has a finite culture window and a limited number of matched conditions; it cannot simply be expanded while retaining the same original neighbourhood. Ladan's group described viability for up to a week. These are practical preparation contrasts, not a universal numerical throughput ranking or an assumption that every organoid survives freezing. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2017.11.010 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/

anchors.text: The useful trade-off is preserved biology against time and repeatability. A characterised PDX supports growth under whole-animal dosing, usually on a months-long establishment clock. Expanded organoids support repeated direct tumour-cell experiments and panels, often over weeks; conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune cells, while Neal's specialised method retained them. A short-term fragment may preserve resident neighbours for a local-interaction question over days, but their function must be demonstrated. No preparation is universally more predictive because it is more complex. Sources: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2018.11.021 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4167608/

anchors.text: The clocks and take rates below belong to different studies. Hidalgo's review described four to eight months to a study-ready PDX. Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 establishment and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to drug exposure, with tumour-type variation: 85 percent in colorectal specimens and 30 percent in breast specimens in that series. Cartry reported a 61.5 percent core-biopsy take rate and six-week median, range four to ten weeks, to a 25-drug colorectal organoid panel. Boileve reported 54/87 establishment (62 percent) and mean 6.8 weeks to a pancreatic chemogram. Ladan used three-day exposures and stated that results can be known in seven to fourteen days; this is a planned window, not an observed turnaround distribution. There were 23/30 usable tests from tumour-containing biopsies. The PDX paper reports 49 percent for 578/1,163; direct count arithmetic is approximately 49.7 percent.

anchors.text: Ladan's breast-slice pilot found 15/20 category matches (75 percent; reported confidence interval 53 to 89 percent), against a pre-set target of at least 55 percent, between the ex vivo anthracycline assay and MRI response after four courses of anthracycline-containing treatment. Both systems used sensitive, intermediate and resistant categories, and neither observed a resistant tumour. Of five disagreements, three were ex vivo sensitive with intermediate MRI response and two the reverse. Among the 23 successful laboratory tests, six were sensitive and 17 intermediate; among the 20 MRI comparisons, four were sensitive and 16 intermediate. This leaves resistance detection untested rather than established. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/

anchors.text: Other agreement measures answer different questions. Vlachogiannis reported 88 percent positive and 100 percent negative predictive values in 21 drug-response comparisons in heavily pretreated gastrointestinal cancers. Boileve reported 83.3 percent sensitivity and 92.9 percent specificity in 34 evaluable pretreated pancreatic patients. Izumchenko compared 129 treatments across 92 patients: 112/129 agreement grouped stable disease with partial and complete responses, while exact-category agreement was 91/129. These endpoints and selected denominators cannot be ranked as head-to-head accuracy or taken as proof that model-guided care improves survival.

anchors.text: Voabil's primary abstract reports that immune-cell reactivation after ex vivo PD-1 blockade in patient-derived tumour fragments predicted clinical response in that study, with perturbation analyses identifying tumour-resident T cells as a key component. This supports a scoped fragment/immune-interaction example, not evidence that choosing treatment from a fragment test improves outcomes. A near-term decision may rule out establishing a new conventional PDX, but does not guarantee a usable fragment; immune presence, movement, recognition and killing remain distinct measurements. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-021-01398-3

It does not show that every organoid line or fresh tumour fragment can be frozen, recovered and retested with unchanged properties. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/

anchors.text: In a wholly fictional development project, D0 supplies one verified malignant preparation. Drug A asks about a direct repair perturbation: a tumour-only organoid supplies a viable-cell count after 48 hours, with division and death measured separately. The invented exposure series is 0.1, 0.3 and 1 micromoles per litre with three wells per condition and vehicle, positive and mechanism controls. Antibody B instead needs compatible tumour and immune populations over a stipulated seven days, with tumour-only, immune-only, matched antibody or carrier, and recognition controls. B's concentration and schedule are missing. The conventional graft's mouse exposure, schedule, assessment day and controls are also missing, so it remains an incomplete proposal. These conditions are not doses established as safe or achievable in people.

anchors.text: A separate fictional three-week decision exercise names real drugs but invents every result. A tumour-only organoid can test a direct olaparib response using an attributed living-cell count after five days; it cannot supply the T cells needed for the pembrolizumab question. Fresh fragments retaining functional resident T cells or a characterised compatible co-culture can address a two-day activation question, with attributed tumour-cell death and recognition controls still needed. A conventional graft cannot restore an intact human immune system and its establishment may miss the deadline. Predicting RNA after BRCA1 loss is a computational hypothesis, not a performed drug exposure. Confirm the actual assay clock: a colorectal six-week median does not forecast the timing for this fictional breast specimen. No choice supplies complete human metabolism, healthy-organ toxicity or every original tumour population.

anchors.text: A virtual cell is a computational model of specified aspects of cells. Its outputs and evaluation depend on the task, training data and model version. scGen combined variational autoencoders with latent-space vector arithmetic and was reported to model perturbation and infection responses across cell types, studies and species, having noted that generalisation to phenomena absent from training data had not previously been shown (Lotfollahi and colleagues, 2019). A 2025 benchmark found that none of five single-cell foundation models and two other deep-learning models predicted transcriptome changes after single or double gene perturbations better than deliberately simple baselines; for most genes the predictions of scGPT, UCE and scBERT did not vary across perturbations, and those of GEARS and scFoundation varied considerably less than the observed values (Ahlmann-Eltze and colleagues, 2025). An AI virtual cell is described as a multi-scale, multi-modal large neural network model in a perspective that sets priorities for accelerating discoveries and guiding experiments, not a validation (Bunne and colleagues, 2024).

anchors.text: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The task defines what an output means: filling a missing RNA value from an image, estimating a drug response and predicting a gene-disruption response are different tasks, and success at one does not validate another. A virtual perturbation changes a model input and calculates an output; it is not a performed experiment, and masking a gene value is not the same as removing the gene's function. Predicted RNA is not measured RNA, protein activity or patient benefit. Agreement summarised across all genes can conceal poor prediction of the few genes that changed, so compare against simple baselines on the genes that moved. An association learned from untreated tissue does not by itself identify a causal drug effect. Whether a model's output supports treatment selection needs separate intended-use clinical evidence, whereas prioritising experiments is a lesser claim.

To claim a drug response, define the intervention and outcome, reserve independent measured experiments, and compare with baselines and the measured response.

Evaluation: what was held out, the baselines, error measures and external data. Failure modes: leakage, incompatible inputs, context shift or the wrong endpoint. Cannot establish alone: a performed perturbation, complete cell biology or better clinical outcomes.

This computational result can prioritise a measured experiment; it supplies neither protein effects, immune interactions, safe delivery nor clinical benefit.

Composition and function change with sampling, cutting, diffusion, medium and time. A retained vessel does not demonstrate perfusion, and visible immune cells do not establish the required interaction. Ladan's breast-slice assay and Salmon's human lung-slice migration experiments support different questions; neither validates every fragment test or treatment decision.

anchors.text: Preparation and assay card. Input: suitable viable tissue with donor/site/time, collection and transport conditions, dimensions and culture window. Cutting, quality checks and endpoints consume finite material and limit available conditions. Compare baseline quality and untreated or carrier controls with defined exposures. Attribute counts, stain fractions, movement or metabolic signal to the relevant cells, with units, time and denominator. Thresholds are method-specific rather than a universal fragment score. Fragment names the preparation; a drug screen names an experiment it may support. Different pieces from one tumour can contain different populations, so matched treatments still need composition checks.

anchors.text: Primary preparation example. Ladan used 300 micrometre slices and three-day exposure in a defined anthracycline-based assay, measuring morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Diffusion into slices differs from vascular delivery; host metabolic activation, clearance, organ toxicity and new immune recruitment were not recreated. Preparation injury, poor viability, uneven diffusion, changing populations and non-tumour signal can invalidate interpretation. A failed culture is not evidence of clinical resistance. Contamination is another reason for assay failure; short-term response does not establish durable elimination, systemic safety or benefit.

anchors.text: Endpoint and validation example. Ladan reported 23 usable assays among 30 tumour-containing biopsies; three of the 23 did not proceed to the clinical treatment comparison, leaving 20 evaluable patients and 15 concordant MRI comparisons. The agreement compared sensitive, intermediate and resistant categories after four courses of anthracycline-containing chemotherapy; it is not a binary drug-killing rate. The study did not observe an ex vivo resistant group, limiting assessment of resistance detection. Those denominators, assay version and preoperative setting cannot validate another postoperative choice. Salmon measured matrix-associated T-cell location and movement in viable lung-tumour slices, not treatment-selection benefit.

anchors.text: Ladan's real study began with 41 consenting people: three did not undergo biopsy and eight biopsies lacked tumour cells, leaving 30 adequate tumour biopsies. Six assays failed the prespecified baseline-apoptosis criterion and one was lost to infection. Of 23 usable results, three people did not receive the chemotherapy, leaving 20 clinical comparisons. The main-text counts are used here; Table 2's footnote instead mentions two people not receiving chemotherapy. The reported interval for 15/20 agreement was 53 to 89 percent, and the pilot's prespecified target was at least 55 percent. Reaching that target supports further investigation, not a demonstration that using the assay to choose care improves outcomes.

anchors.text: The reported breast-study totals imply two sensitive dish calls with sensitive MRI, three sensitive dish calls with intermediate MRI, two intermediate dish calls with sensitive MRI and thirteen intermediate calls matching MRI. Thus 15/20 agree, including thirteen matches in the common intermediate category. Two of four MRI-sensitive tumours were called sensitive in the dish (50 percent), and two of five sensitive dish calls matched MRI sensitivity (40 percent). These are stated comparisons with an imperfect MRI outcome, not validated sensitivity or positive predictive value against known truth. FDA's March 2007 diagnostic-test guidance distinguishes agreement from accuracy when the comparator is not a reference standard. The study's sensitive category required more than 50 percent size reduction after four chemotherapy courses; it is not simply the standard RECIST partial-response category. anchors.text: Organoids self-organise selected structural or functional tissue features in three-dimensional culture. Patient-derived tumour organoids are one member of this broader family, rather than complete copies of a patient. Establishment and growth conditions select cells, and identity and relevant properties need checking against the source specimen. Conventional epithelial cultures often omit immune and supporting populations; specialised retention or added co-cultures require method-specific evidence. Their use for mechanism and drug-response experiments does not by itself establish clinical utility.

anchors.text: Model and assay card. Starting material may be normal tissue, tumour or stem-cell-derived material; retain its source and viable preservation method. Record malignant identity against the specimen, selected or lost populations, matrix/medium, passage and experimental window. Derivation, quality checks, expansion and testing use finite tissue and culture material. A destructive stain or lysate assay consumes its tested aliquot; recovery in another assay is method-specific. No universal specimen amount or organoid-response threshold follows from the name.

anchors.text: Failure and inference checks. Establishment can fail, normal epithelial cells can overgrow malignant cells, and culture conditions can select branches. Verify tumour identity rather than infer it from growth. Output belongs to the chosen assay: attributed cell counts, death-marker fraction or molecular signal, with units, time and normalisation. Check viability, composition, exposure and controls. A three-dimensional spheroid need not show tissue-like self-organisation, and specialised immune retention does not apply to all cultures. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30550791/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10598932/ Dijkstra explicitly checked tumour identity to exclude healthy-lung organoid overgrowth: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6558289/

Adding immune cells creates a new experiment needing identity, persistence and specificity controls. The model can support a direct tumour-cell question while leaving host exposure, organ toxicity and patient benefit untested.

anchors.text: Patient-derived tumour organoids are cultures established from a patient's tumour tissue that can be expanded for repeated laboratory experiments when establishment succeeds. They are one member of the broader organoid family defined on the organoid record; establishment selects cells, malignant identity must be checked against the source specimen, and conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune and supporting populations. Mechanism and drug-response results from them do not by themselves establish clinical utility.

anchors.text: Drug-specific agreement can fail to transfer even within colorectal cancer. Ooft and colleagues reported that organoids predicted the biopsied lesion's response in more than 80 percent of people receiving irinotecan-based treatment, but failed to predict response to fluorouracil plus oxaliplatin. The Netherlands Cancer Institute's 2019 research announcement describes 61 patients in the clinical study; Wensink's later review tabulates 29 people in the response-comparison cohort, including ten receiving irinotecan and twelve receiving an irinotecan doublet. Those cohort and regimen denominators are not interchangeable. This was a prediction comparison, not evidence that assigning treatment by the test improved patient outcomes.

anchors.text: Wensink's 2021 review included seventeen publications, five about colorectal cancer; seven used metastatic populations. Its pooled sensitivity was 81 percent and specificity 74 percent for the included response comparisons. The authors warned that these estimates were likely high because some studies lacked quantitative results needed for pooling and not all used a predefined index test; publication or outcome-reporting bias could not be excluded. The pooled establishment estimate was 68.0 percent at patient level and 68.5 percent at sample level, with heterogeneous studies and wide intervals. These are different quantities from response agreement and from clinical utility. The review also reports a 34-day median just to establish organoids from breast biopsies, distinct from a completed drug panel or an individual decision deadline.

anchors.text: Vlachogiannis and colleagues studied organoids from heavily pretreated metastatic colorectal and gastroesophageal cancers. They grew organoids from 70 percent of adequately cellular biopsies and compared model and clinical drug responses in 21 comparisons. The reported sensitivity was 100 percent, specificity 93 percent, positive predictive value 88 percent and negative predictive value 100 percent for those comparisons. These are the study's response metrics with its defined comparators and selected denominator, not 88 percent accuracy for all patients or evidence for a postoperative breast decision. Culture success, response agreement and benefit from assigning treatment remain separate questions.

anchors.text: Boileve and colleagues prospectively enrolled 87 people with pretreated advanced pancreatic cancer, generated 54 organoids (62 percent) and had 34 evaluable patients with clinical follow-up. The 34 evaluable people are about 39 percent of the original 87, not 39 percent of successful cultures. Mean time to a chemogram was 6.8 weeks; reported sensitivity was 83.3 percent and specificity 92.9 percent. Those selected results and routine-care hit versus nonhit comparisons do not establish a randomised treatment-selection benefit or validate a breast-cancer assay.

anchors.text: Functional drug testing exposes a defined living preparation to medicines and measures a specified response. Preparations may use dissociated cells, expanded organoids or short-term tissue cultures. Feasibility, outcome agreement and benefit from using a result to choose care are separate questions and must be tied to the actual assay version, cancer, treatment and setting.

anchors.text: Specimen and assay card. Record donor/site/time, living preparation, transport and processing, initial composition, culture history, assay version, concentrations, exposure duration, replicates and control range. Fixed tissue cannot supply living cells; whether previously frozen material can supply the required viable preparation must be demonstrated for that protocol. Input suitability and recovery must be demonstrated for the method. Testing and endpoint processing use finite material. Output needs units, denominator, normalisation and uncertainty; acceptance criteria must be defined for the actual method. Name whether the preparation is dissociated cells, a fresh fragment or an expanded organoid. Mixed samples include normal neighbours, and expansion can change the represented populations.

anchors.text: Handling evidence is method-specific. Ladan and colleagues collected breast tissue in their specified medium, cut 300 micrometre slices and assessed morphology, proliferation and apoptosis after three-day exposure. This is not a general transport or storage protocol for all screens. Growth-rate methods show why baseline counts and control division affect interpretation. Retain failures and exclusions; failed preparation is not clinical resistance. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ Medium, drug access and exposure duration can change the result. Mechanism-relevant controls test whether the claimed interaction can occur; absent required cells or unrealistic exposures can make an experiment uninformative even when a numerical response is available. A laboratory concentration is not a safe human dose.

anchors.text: Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

anchors.text: Restivo and colleagues generated organoids from matched fresh and slow-frozen colorectal tumour tissue from two patients with stage IV disease. Their specified slow-freezing protocol used a cryoprotectant to preserve living material, and the frozen-derived cultures took longer to form than the fresh-derived cultures. This is evidence of recovery under that protocol, not equivalence of all fresh, snap-frozen and viable-cryopreserved samples or a guaranteed turnaround. The handling history, recovery, malignant identity and assay quality need checking for the intended experiment. Preserved molecular material alone does not establish a recoverable living model. Source: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-022-04025-0

anchors.text: Read a model study as a sequence of explicitly defined groups: people or specimens offered or submitted, preparations yielding a usable model, results compared with a clinical outcome, and results agreeing under the stated rule. Eligibility exclusions, absent tumour, laboratory failures, missing outcomes and people not receiving the treatment belong to different steps. State whether the unit is a person, specimen or treatment comparison; one person can contribute more than one. A percentage among compared cases cannot describe everyone originally offered testing, and an analysis exclusion is not automatically a failed culture. Keep the drug, cancer, treatment history, outcome, clock and assay version attached rather than ranking different studies as competing accuracy scores.

anchors.text: The prospective single-arm SENSOR study enrolled 61 people with metastatic colorectal cancer: 54 were eligible, 31 organoids were generated, 25 cultures were screened against eight drugs and nineteen showed a substantial laboratory response. Six people received an organoid-selected treatment, three vistusertib and three capivasertib, with no objective clinical responses. That observation concerns this panel and selected population; it neither establishes benefit from using the assay nor proves that every organoid method is ineffective. Guillen and colleagues' breast-model report describes a complete response in one person with metastatic triple-negative disease after a model-nominated treatment. That case demonstrates feasibility, without a comparison estimating how often the strategy helps.

anchors.text: Randomised outcome evidence must be assessed for the named assay and use rather than declared absent for all functional testing in solid tumours. Ranjan and colleagues reported a 2023 trial of ChemoID selection versus physician choice from the same chemotherapy list in 78 people with recurrent glioblastoma under the 2016 WHO definition. Enrolment stopped after a prespecified efficacy analysis; the intention-to-treat report gave median overall survival of twelve versus 7.5 months. Participants could provide viable tumour through surgery or biopsy, so the findings do not include every patient with recurrent glioblastoma. Cordgenics supported the assay resources, and two authors declared licensed intellectual-property interests. This is evidence for the studied strategy and population, without validating another assay, organoid system, postoperative breast decision or universal treatment rule.

anchors.text: Ex vivo blood-cancer screening measures a specified response in collected malignant and comparator populations. Results depend on the specimen, preparation, treatment exposure and assay. The EXALT study is one clinical investigation of a defined selection approach; a screen result alone does not establish a safe treatment, and failed or uninterpretable experiments are not clinical resistance findings. Generalisation to another cancer, assay or decision strategy requires separate evidence.

anchors.text: The prospective EXALT study tested an image-based single-cell selection approach in 143 people with advanced aggressive blood cancers. Fifty-six were treated according to the assay; 30 of those 56 (54 percent) had progression-free survival at least 1.3 times that on their own previous therapy. The comparator was each person's prior therapy in a single-arm study, not randomised standard care. This result does not show that all tested patients benefited or validate another assay or disease setting. Source: https://doi.org/10.1158/2159-8290.CD-21-0538

anchors.text: EXALT used viable material from blood, bone marrow or lymph nodes. These are method- and disease-specific inputs, not evidence that every blood cancer is easy to sample or that its test transfers to a solid-tumour preparation. The 143 enrolled and tested people, 56 receiving assay-guided therapy and 30 meeting the PFS-ratio endpoint remain distinct groups. The comparator for that endpoint was each person's previous therapy; another twenty people formed a physician-choice observational cohort, without random allocation.

anchors.text: A patient-derived xenograft starts with patient tumour material implanted into another species, commonly an immunodeficient mouse. It can retain relevant tumour features within a different host, while engraftment selects populations and mouse-derived support can replace human stroma and vessels. Whole-animal dosing includes mouse exposure and metabolism, not human physiology. Humanised models add selected components whose identity, compatibility and persistence need checking. Fidelity and patient prediction are question- and method-specific.

anchors.text: Timing and denominators. Hidalgo's 2014 review described four to eight months to a study-ready model; it is a historical review estimate, not a laboratory guarantee. Izumchenko's series reported 578 successful grafts from 1,163 implanted specimens, described as 49 percent, and a mean 16 weeks from engraftment to drug exposure, with substantial variation. That clock is not the whole biopsy-to-decision interval. Keep submitted, established and interpretable donor models separate. Arithmetic check by OnCo: 578 divided by 1,163 is approximately 49.7 percent; the paper itself states 49 percent. Retain the counts and distinguish the reported percentage from this calculation. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4167608/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5834154/
