anchors.text: Fidelity is measured, not assumed. Record histology, lineage and relevant molecular features against the source, host strain, site and passage, and species assignment for the mechanism. Ben-David reported mouse-specific copy-number evolution in studied datasets; Woo's direct-DNA analyses reported conservation and showed that measurement method matters. Neither establishes perfect preservation nor inevitable complete divergence for every model. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28991255/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7808565/ Engraftment is establishment of growth after implantation; passage transfers an established graft to another host. Reduced growth relative to a control is different from regression below a stated starting burden. Matching molecular features does not validate every drug prediction.

anchors.text: Assay card. Viable material, establishment, passage and animal experiments consume finite material. Report burden or volume with units, baseline and observation clock, exposure and comparator animals, and donor versus animal counts. Failed engraftment and excluded experiments remain visible. Human-specific binding to tumour cells does not establish activity on mouse stromal targets. A graft tested later in a dish has a different experimental setting. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3553601/

Its procedures and material types are repository-specific. Yang's 2026 primary abstract describes adding patient-derived tumour and mesenchymal cells, human endothelial cells and humanised marrow to a specialised immune-stroma PDX. This is evidence for a defined added-component model, not complete reconstruction of human immunity. anchors.text: Izumchenko and colleagues compared 129 treatments across 92 people with advanced solid tumours. Their 112/129 agreement figure (87 percent) grouped stable disease with partial and complete responses as positive disease control; reported sensitivity was 96 percent and specificity 70 percent. Requiring the exact RECIST category instead gave 91/129 agreement (71 percent). Responses came from the consulting oncologist and from xenograft volume changes converted to RECIST equivalents. These selected, repeated treatment comparisons are not 129 independent people, a head-to-head accuracy ranking against other model types or a trial showing benefit from assigning treatment by the model.

anchors.text: A controlled perturbation deliberately changes a defined factor and measures the response against appropriate comparison conditions. Vehicle, positive, negative and mechanism controls answer different questions. A reproducible response can support an experimental claim without establishing its proposed mechanism or patient benefit. Baseline growth, timing, dose and the actual unit assigned to treatment matter.

anchors.text: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

anchors.text: Keep what changed, the comparator, concentration or dose range, timing, assignment, readout and units, sample identities, replicate structure and variability. Repeated wells address variation under their preparation and allocation; independently obtained biological samples address another source of variation. Many wells from one tumour do not become independent patients, and repetition or a small p-value does not repair a missing comparison. A two-drug experiment needs vehicle, both single drugs and the combination. A larger combination effect than either single drug is not automatically synergy; that claim needs a stated reference model.

anchors.text: Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

anchors.text: A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

anchors.text: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

anchors.text: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

anchors.text: In vitro and ex vivo describe work outside the original organism, with terminology varying by preparation and expansion. In vivo refers to work within a living organism, including animals and people; in silico refers to computation. Each setting includes different components and omits others. The label does not establish a universal ranking, human safety or treatment benefit.

anchors.text: Setting comparison. In vitro describes laboratory work outside the body, including grown cells and many expanded organoid assays. Ex vivo commonly describes removed living material studied outside its original organism, often briefly with retained local structure. Authors use overlapping terminology, so inspect preparation, expansion and timing. In vivo includes experiments in animals or people; identify species and host. In silico computes a prediction from data rather than directly measuring the predicted response. These terms describe where and how the experiment occurs, not a quality ranking.

anchors.text: Read each omitted compartment. A tumour-only dish lacks required immune interactions unless those populations are added and shown functional. A fresh slice may retain resident neighbours while losing blood flow and recruitment from circulation. A conventional PDX adds mouse circulation, exposure and metabolism without reproducing an intact human immune system. A computational prediction depends on its data, assumptions and benchmark. Human-derived tissue can be used in both dish and animal models; do not claim that ex vivo is the only setting using human tissue. A living specimen can lose cells, adapt or undergo selection after removal; retaining a structure is not retaining complete physiology. In-vitro preparations can isolate direct effects, compare doses and drugs and support repeats, while omitting perfused blood supply, host metabolism and the original population mix unless specifically reconstructed. Latin labels such as in glass, out of the living and in the living are mnemonics for setting, not quality grades.

anchors.text: Primary timing examples. Ladan's breast-slice assay used three-day exposures, a stated planned result window of seven to fourteen days, not a measured turnaround distribution and 23/30 usable tests from tumour-containing biopsies. Izumchenko reported 578/1,163 established PDXs and mean 16 weeks from engraftment to exposure, not biopsy to final decision. Ahlmann-Eltze compared gene-perturbation transcriptome predictions with simple baselines; the deep-learning methods did not outperform the simple linear baselines in the tested expression-prediction tasks. This was not a measured patient drug response. None of these examples shows benefit from choosing a treatment using the model. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5834154/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40759747/

That return step distinguishes cell-engineering procedures from laboratory drug testing where the tested sample is not returned. Dosing an animal and later treating removed graft cells in a dish are different experiments. Source: https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/ex-vivo

anchors.text: Regulatory scope. FDA's roadmap to reduce animal testing concerns preclinical safety development, initially focusing on monoclonal antibodies and considering human-based laboratory and computational methods. It is not approval of every organ chip or a recommendation for personal treatment selection. Source: https://www.fda.gov/files/newsroom/published/roadmap_to_reducing_animal_testing_in_preclinical_safety_studies.pdf Decision time limits which preparation is usable: establishing a new conventional PDX generally will not fit a decision due in three weeks, while a characterised short-term assay might fit but can still fail. A treatment needing liver activation also needs the relevant metabolic setting represented; a fresh slice alone omits it. Computation can rank hypotheses without growing a model, but a universal fastest or cheapest claim is not established by the setting label.

anchors.text: Fictional reading exercise. Compare a graft dosed in a mouse, a fresh human slice exposed outside the body and a computed sensitivity prediction. Identify actual measurement versus prediction, host, retained cells, omitted physiology and clock before drawing an inference. These settings can start from the same tumour; days, weeks or months are illustrative scales rather than guaranteed timelines. No setting is a later validation rung of another.

anchors.text: An experimental setting and the origin of the material are separate descriptions. Human-derived cells can be studied in vitro, briefly ex vivo or as a graft in vivo. Living-organism work includes animals and people; it does not automatically mean a human clinical trial. Preclinical intervention experiments can continue alongside human studies, so the date relative to a first human dose alone does not validate their treatment claim.

anchors.text: Analytical validity, clinical validity and clinical utility address different questions for a specified assay, specimen, population and intended use. MedlinePlus Genetics distinguishes detection of a genetic variant, its relationship to disease presence or risk, and whether the information helps diagnosis, treatment, management or prevention. Reliable measurement does not by itself establish clinical meaning, and an outcome association does not establish benefit from changing care. For a prediction model, reproducibility of fixed-input output, discrimination, calibrated probabilities and the consequences of model-guided decisions also require distinct evidence. These are related questions rather than a universal sequence that guarantees a useful test.

anchors.text: Start a claim worksheet with the population and treatment setting, specimen and method version, measured or predicted outcome, time horizon and proposed decision. A molecule measurement, drug ranking in a dish and outcome prediction from earlier patients are different claims. For risk, retain whether the estimate assumes usual care or no treatment; for a drug experiment, retain the drug, dose and combination. Leave unavailable details unknown. Then separate the tested material and quality, biological interpretation and alternatives, prediction, proposed action and evidence of benefit. Mark each measured, inferred, proposed or unknown. A sound measurement does not automatically support the later steps.

anchors.text: Consider a fictional report that calls a protein-rich stored tumour a Drug A responder. Its study related protein abundance to shrinkage among people all receiving Drug A for advanced Cancer X. The measurement and response association can be useful, but there is no untreated or alternative-treatment comparison establishing greater benefit from A. Applying it after surgery also changes the setting. Ask what comparison shows improved outcomes from choosing A with this result in the proposed setting. Confirmation of protein abundance answers whether that signal is real, while postoperative benefit remains a separate question. A favourable prognostic result does not itself justify omitting standard treatment.

anchors.text: An evidence card records population, stage, treatment context and selection; specimen, handling, assay version and quality criteria; the reference condition or care comparator and its limitations; outcome and measurement time; the analysis plan, all tuning and independent evaluation; failed samples, dropout and missing outcomes; and sample size, intervals and remaining uncertainty. A response endpoint is not recurrence or survival. A preclinical card names the actual model and tested claim; an observational clinical association retains possible confounding. Neither alone establishes that the proposed clinical action helps. A headline metric also needs the consequences of false positive and false negative calls attached to the action. Distinguish prespecified analyses from exploratory searches, keep their tuning history, and seek confirmation that does not reuse the search. State whether a treatment-study denominator includes everyone assigned, only those treated or only those evaluable.

anchors.text: For analytical performance, request the detection limit with its target level, input amount, specimen and detection probability; precision within runs and across days, operators, instruments and reagent lots; agreement with an appropriate independent reference; attempted-sample failure rate and reasons; and specimen handling, preservation and interference testing. The 2017 AMP/CAP recommendations concern next-generation sequencing panels for somatic variants. They ask for performance by variant class and relevant reference materials, depth and sample numbers. They describe a lower detection limit at which 95 per cent of samples are reliably detected, but also explain why observing 19 or 20 successes in 20 trials does not by itself establish that reliability with confidence. This is an assay-specific example, not a universal validation protocol. Fresh and delayed specimens can differ, and measurement variation must be understood before interpreting a trend. Self-agreement alone does not establish accuracy.

anchors.text: Put the decision before ordering. Write what positive, negative, uncertain and failed results would change, including proposed treatment omission, confirmation or another sample. Compare existing pathology and other tests, and record the decision deadline, finite tissue, time, travel, uncertainty and financial burden. Name who interprets the result, who owns the clinical recommendation and when further testing is unlikely to help that decision. A result arriving after the decision closes may not serve its intended use. The worksheet exposes assumptions rather than calculating a treatment choice; urgency does not establish validity.

anchors.text: In the fictional postoperative protein-test case, possible next steps are checking the actual companion-diagnostic requirement and whether this assay meets it, inspecting the Drug A evidence, considering a trial of the relevant strategy, or declining a tissue-consuming test that would not change the decision. The exact laboratory, service, version and intended use matter. A research-use label, laboratory certification, development designation or report drug list cannot replace the claim-specific evidence. A companion test is tied to specified treatment use. Clinician-led off-label use, access, payment and suitability are additional questions, not promises made by a molecular report. Fast-track and breakthrough-therapy designations are not marketing approval; accelerated approval is a distinct approval pathway, not just a development designation.

anchors.text: Research can have a defined value without selecting treatment: checking a mechanism, explaining discordant assays or generating a future hypothesis. Name the reviewer and what would count as a useful answer rather than extending an endless chain of tests. Attribute unpublished company data and state which methods and results were available to inspect; unavailable evidence does not prove the claim false. In a fictional high/low recurrence-risk test for which neither answer changes recommended care and no relevant study is open, the immediate value for that treatment decision is limited. A separate research or personal-information goal should be weighed against burden, uncertainty and alternatives. A changed treatment decision is not itself demonstrated benefit and can add unnecessary treatment.

anchors.text: A cell line arises through subculture of an initial primary culture. Finite lines have limited proliferative capacity; continuous lines can proliferate for prolonged periods under suitable conditions. Continuous growth does not itself establish malignancy. Lines may attach to surfaces or grow in suspension. Their source, passage history, medium and density shape the selected population. Cancer-line strains can diverge genetically and in drug response, so a familiar name does not guarantee identical biology across laboratories.

anchors.text: Model card. Input: documented banked cells or viable material used to establish a culture. Record source and version, medium, density, passage and relevant phenotype. Output belongs to the chosen assay, such as counts, doubling time in hours or a death fraction with its denominator. Passage counts transfers, not a fixed number of divisions. Identity matching by human short tandem repeat profiling, mycoplasma testing and phenotype/growth checks address different questions. Establishment can fail or select subsets; no line-name cutoff predicts clinical sensitivity. Sources: https://www.atcc.org/resources/culture-guides/animal-cell-culture-guide ; https://www.atcc.org/-/media/resources/technical-documents/cell-line-authentication-test-recommendations.pdf?rev=7664fa886e5948018dfe198d484bb4eb Establishing a new line uses finite viable tissue and can select populations. A cell line need not be a monolayer. ATCC uses authentication broadly for verification of identity and freedom from contamination: short tandem repeat profiling compares repeated DNA stretches to test human-line identity, while mycoplasma and other contamination tests and relevant phenotype checks answer additional questions. Passing the identity test does not answer all of them.

Check identity, contamination and matched conditions before attributing the difference to one cause. Replicate wells assess a preparation, not independent donors. anchors.text: A simple characterised line is useful for isolating a mechanism, comparing many perturbations and repeating an experiment. Its missing architecture, host drug handling and normal-tissue responses limit the inference, and a tumour-only line cannot test an immune interaction without the required added populations. A more elaborate culture changes selected ingredients; it does not create a universal hierarchy of reliability.

anchors.text: Cancer cell lines are selected populations maintained in culture. Versions of the same named line can differ genetically and in drug response. The culture does not reproduce the whole tumour, host drug handling or complete immune environment. Transfer to patients therefore depends on the intended intervention, endpoint, population and validation evidence, rather than the line name alone.

anchors.text: A suspended microchannel resonator weighs a cell relative to the fluid it displaces using the shift in a vibrating beam's frequency. Buoyant mass equals cell volume multiplied by the difference between cell and fluid density. It is not simply diameter or dry mass. Repeatedly measuring the same cell estimates mass accumulation rate; Godin reversed the flow to reintroduce the same cell to the sensor (a dynamic trap) and Cermak used serial sensors along one channel. Stevens investigated drug-response associations in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples, rather than universal clinical prediction.

anchors.text: Assay card. Input: viable cells compatible with suspension and channel handling. Record source, identity, preparation losses, fluid and temperature conditions, exposure and observation interval. Calibration maps frequency shifts to mass, often picograms. Tracking repeated readings estimates a slope, often picograms per hour; mass-normalised rates have inverse-time units. Preparation and exposure consume finite material; the physical measurement can preserve cells, but recovery and downstream compatibility depend on the method.

anchors.text: Quality and inference. Check clumps, cell attribution, instrument drift, calibration, tracking ambiguity and sufficient linked readings. Serial-sensor analyses exclude uncertain matches rather than invent a trajectory. Fluid-density changes can change buoyant mass. A small positive slope still indicates accumulation in the observed interval; later recovery, death and resistance need additional endpoints and time. Many measured cells from one specimen are not many independent patients. No universal rate cutoff establishes clinical sensitivity or immune recognition. Buoyant mass is also not a count of cell divisions. Physical measurement performance, a reproducible drug-response association and validated use for a clinical decision are separate kinds of evidence. Without extra measurements or assumptions, this sensor does not establish dry mass, a death mechanism, immune specificity or patient benefit.

anchors.text: Fictional arithmetic. A tracked cell rising from 10 to 12 picograms over one hour has a slope of 2 picograms per hour. Comparable groups at 2 and 0.5 picograms per hour differ by (2 minus 0.5) divided by 2, or 75 percent. Both rates are positive. This is a rate reduction, not shrinkage, a killed-cell fraction or patient response. These values are invented.

anchors.text: The positive research use is a rapid physical response readout and a view of cell-to-cell variation that a population average can conceal. Stevens measured short-term mass accumulation in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples; this can precede a large endpoint-count change, while slower accumulation can occur in living cells. A mixed specimen still requires attribution to the relevant population, and a mass sensor does not supply immune cells or recognition. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5142231/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5064867/

anchors.text: In pooled CRISPR knockout screens, guide sequences track perturbed populations over time. Relative enrichment or depletion supports a fitness effect under the experimental conditions, including proliferation and survival. Guide delivery and editing efficiency, representation, unintended effects and copy-number-dependent cutting can confound interpretation. Independent perturbations and appropriate follow-up strengthen on-target attribution. Knockout and drug inhibition differ in extent, activity and duration, so a genetic hit does not establish a clinically useful drug.

anchors.text: Some dependencies are shared broadly and others enriched in a particular lineage or genomic context. A gene needed by normal cells may limit therapeutic selectivity. Knockout can remove a protein, whereas a drug may inhibit only one activity partly or temporarily. Guide abundance after perturbation is not RNA expression, and a negative gene-effect score follows the analysis convention rather than guaranteeing drug sensitivity. No screen alone establishes normal-tissue safety. In a fictional amplified-region example, a strong depletion signal becomes small after cutting-toxicity correction; the original rank alone cannot nominate an inhibitor. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5709193/

anchors.text: External evaluation applies an existing model to data outside its development and compares predictions with observed outcomes. The TRIPOD-Cluster explanation includes later-period data collected by the same investigators as well as data from another hospital, country or care setting. A different platform is not a universal requirement. Apparent performance uses the development data and can be optimistic. Internal validation with resampling can estimate optimism and performance for new people from the same source population; it is evidence about a different question, rather than no result. External evaluation quantifies performance and its uncertainty instead of conferring a universal pass or fail. Keep the locked method, population, outcome, follow-up and differences from development visible.

anchors.text: Follow the people behind a performance plot: eligibility, selection, care, sample quality, failures and missing outcomes. Identify every variable-selection, preprocessing and threshold choice and whether outcomes were known when those choices were made. Good performance on ideal specimens or the development patients may not describe practice. External evaluation uses data outside development, which can differ in hospital, calendar period, handling or care. The data and evaluation need to be independent of the tuning decisions; a new company logo supplies no such guarantee.

anchors.text: Two fictional slides illustrate the boundary. Slide A uses Hospital A patients and their known outcomes to select variables and a threshold, then reports performance on those same A patients. That is apparent performance; repeating the computation can check reproducibility without providing a new independent population test. Slide B fixes preprocessing, variables and threshold using A before applying the locked method to separate Hospital B patients. It reports B performance and the failed-test denominator, with no B outcomes fed back into tuning. This supports evaluation outside development, while suitable population, uncertainty, calibration and usefulness of clinical decisions remain separate questions. The patient icons are schematic and neither slide supplies a measured performance value.

anchors.text: A model evaluated at a second hospital may still address advanced treated disease rather than the proposed postoperative use. Discrimination asks whether outcomes are ranked usefully; calibration asks whether stated probabilities agree with observed frequencies in comparable groups. Good ranking can coexist with inflated risk estimates, and good prognostic probabilities do not establish benefit from a treatment printed beside them. There is no single performance cutoff that makes every decision appropriate. If unchanged Hospital A samples are rerun, request an evaluation set held out from every tuning choice, a locked method, target population and outcome, all failure denominators and uncertainty. Internal resampling and independent external evaluation answer different performance questions; neither name alone is a clinical-use verdict.

anchors.text: In statistics and machine learning, leakage is the use of information during training that would not be available at prediction time, which produces overly optimistic performance estimates (Wikipedia). Common cancer-data forms are normalising or selecting genes on the full cohort before splitting, duplicated patients across TCGA and cBioPortal studies, and benchmark contamination, where a foundation model's pretraining corpus contained the public test set (TCGA slides or profiles), so that its downstream score is partly recall.

anchors.text: Bioprinting controls deposition of biological materials to build an experimental construct. The printing plan, measured final geometry, viable cells and biological function are distinct evidence. Kolesky and colleagues printed cell-containing and removable inks, removed the temporary channel material, added endothelial lining and perfused engineered tissues. This tissue-engineering experiment did not demonstrate a complete human organ or cancer-treatment utility. Yi and colleagues reported a particular glioblastoma chip combining patient-derived tumour cells, endothelial cells and brain-derived matrix; its abstract supports that bounded example.

anchors.text: Chip devices can control selected cells, matrix, interfaces, transport or mechanical conditions. Their composition varies: channels do not automatically supply endothelium or immune cells. Huh's lung model separated alveolar and vascular compartments and imposed mechanical strain; Hassell studied lung cancer in defined engineered environments. Jenkins placed immune-containing organotypic spheroids in a collagen microfluidic compartment. These are capabilities of particular systems, not universal chip properties or validation for personal treatment selection.

anchors.text: Co-culture studies interactions among defined populations. Dijkstra and colleagues combined autologous blood lymphocytes with tumour organoids from mismatch repair-deficient colorectal cancer and from non-small-cell lung cancer, with enrichment and later killing measurements as separate stages. Neal and colleagues retained native immune components using a specialised air-liquid-interface organoid method. Presence, activation, tumour recognition and killing require different observations; neither model label establishes universal patient prediction.

anchors.text: Positive predictive value is the proportion of positive test calls that meet a specified reference condition: true positives divided by true plus false positives. A positive result can be a true positive or a false positive; a false positive is a positive call in someone without that reference condition. Negative predictive value uses negative calls as its denominator. These differ from sensitivity and specificity, which start with reference-condition groups. The population base rate, reference standard, threshold and actual assay performance determine how the fractions should be interpreted.

anchors.text: A proportion identifies an outcome within a defined group. The denominator might be everyone enrolled, everyone treated, people with an evaluable scan, or only people with a recurrence; those answer different questions. Conditional probability makes the specified group explicit and is not a statement of causation. Repeated measurements do not create new independent people. Unknown outcomes and incomplete follow-up require explicit handling rather than being silently treated as measured non-response.

anchors.text: Pharmacokinetics describes absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion. A dose is an administered amount; exposure describes a named substance's concentration over time in a specified compartment. Route, organ function, metabolism, binding and interactions can make equal doses produce different exposure.

anchors.text: A case report documents a clinical course, interventions, outcomes and alternative explanations. It can reveal a signal of benefit or harm without establishing what would have happened under another approach. The CARE reporting guideline includes a timeline, diagnostic assessment, interventions, follow-up, the patient perspective and consent; complete reporting supports appraisal rather than proving treatment causation.

anchors.text: A trial defines primary, secondary and exploratory outcomes and how they are measured and analysed. The primary question informs design, sample size and testing; having a secondary endpoint does not by itself establish whether it was adequately powered or met a prespecified testing rule. Overall survival concerns death from any cause, while response, progression, symptoms and quality of life answer different questions. A composite endpoint combines specified events, so its definition and starting time matter. FDA's December 2018 nonbinding oncology-endpoint guidance distinguishes direct clinical benefit and context-dependent surrogate evidence; use in an approval does not make an endpoint interchangeable with survival in every setting.

anchors.text: A study question card keeps the population and setting, prior treatment and exclusions, complete intervention and comparator, endpoint definition and assessment, starting clock and horizon together. The intervention may be a sequence of medicines, procedures and surgery. Read the protocol and analysis plan for treatment stopping, switching and missing outcomes. A percentage without these details may answer a different question from the proposed action.

anchors.text: A marker can be associated with a later outcome without being validated as a substitute for it. For treatment-effect surrogacy, the question is whether changes caused by treatment in the proposed surrogate predict changes in the outcome of interest. Trial-level validation examines treatment effects across suitable randomised studies, with attention to disease, treatment class, endpoint and intended outcome. A patient-level association alone cannot establish that relationship.

anchors.text: A surrogate is a measured outcome used in place of a direct clinical-benefit outcome, with evidence needed for that substitution in the intended setting. Two relationships must be separated: people with a favourable marker may have better outcomes, while treatments that improve that marker may or may not improve the outcome. The first is a prognostic association; the second concerns agreement between treatment effects across suitable randomised comparisons. A treatment can change another pathway, later disease or toxicity as well as the marker. Validation is specific to disease, treatment context and intended outcome. An early measure is not automatically validated, and regulatory acceptance in one programme does not transfer to another. “Validated” and “reasonably likely to predict benefit” carry different evidence claims. Even a pathology or imaging response does not capture every benefit and harm.

anchors.text: For target lesions, partial response requires at least a 30 percent decrease from the baseline sum.

anchors.text: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. Blood-cancer studies can use cell-based or molecular measurements, while solid-tumour studies can look for tumour-associated features in plasma. The disease, specimen, technique, time point and threshold define the result. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that method, not proof that every cancer cell is absent. Associations with recurrence, benefit from a test-guided treatment strategy, and validation of a surrogate endpoint are separate questions; evidence for one setting does not establish the others.

anchors.text: A circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) assay looks for tumour-associated features in a finite sample of cell-free DNA. How much tumour DNA reaches the sampled blood varies between lesions, and recovery, background DNA, the features tracked and the assay's detection limit all shape the call. Imaging measures a defined region through a physical signal. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the breast can report contrast enhancement or the volume of enhancing tissue, which is not a direct count of viable cancer cells. The two tests can therefore differ without either being wrong, and neither automatically replaces the other.

Imaging alone cannot count viable tumour cells, and enhancement can have more than one tissue cause. Neither agreement nor disagreement shows that a treatment change would help, which is a clinical-utility question.

anchors.text: A randomized trial assigns eligible consenting participants to interventions by chance. Concealing the next assignment protects enrolment against foreknowledge; blinding concerns awareness after assignment. These are different design features. Randomization reduces treatment-selection confounding but leaves possible chance imbalance, missing outcomes and limits on applicability. The comparator, endpoint, analysis and conduct determine what the comparison establishes.

This establishes capabilities of a defined model, not a universal ability to predict clinical treatment benefit. anchors.text: Question-first reading framework. Name the intervention, required cells or processes, endpoint, observation time and intended inference. Predicting a molecular change, culture growth, scan response and benefit from a treatment strategy are different questions. Trust belongs to this question and evidence, not the model name or complexity. Include the consequence of an incorrect answer when deciding how much supporting evidence the use needs.

anchors.text: Construction and readout. Record source and identity, retained or added populations, viable window, preparation/version and missing components. Define measured or predicted object, units, reference and uncertainty. Check relevant controls, baseline growth and population attribution. A lower count than a dividing control is not necessarily a count below the start. Reliability within a run, independent biological specimens and correctness answer different questions. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30550791/ Human-derived cells or tissue are not complete human physiology. Repeatability can preserve a systematic error; a measured treatment effect does not identify its mechanism without comparisons that distinguish alternative explanations.

anchors.text: Prediction and proposed use. Evaluate outcomes not used to build or tune a rule, retain failures, uncertainty and mismatches, and examine relevant baselines. Attach assay version, population, treatment and endpoint to agreement. Ladan's preoperative breast-slice comparison cannot validate an unrelated postoperative drug or assay. Clinical validity and benefit from using a decision strategy remain distinct; the analytical-versus-clinical-validation owner holds that distinction. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/

anchors.text: Fictional example. A tumour-only culture repeatedly responds to Drug A. This does not test an immune-dependent Drug B or prove benefit because the cells came from a patient. Check the required immune interaction, actual intervention, endpoint and independent validation. Repeatability cannot repair a mismatch between question and model. These are invented drugs and a reading exercise. Complexity is useful when it represents biology necessary for the question and remains measurable. A simpler model may isolate a mechanism, while another model is needed for an interaction absent from it. More components alone do not show better prediction.

anchors.text: An original wholly fictional validation exercise uses D0 and its repeated wells only for development, then reserves one pretreatment specimen from each of thirty new donors in an advanced breast-cancer research setting. Lock every fitting, threshold and preprocessing choice before their outcomes. The toy assay counts identified tumour cells after drug A at 0.3 micromoles per litre for 48 hours. Reportability requires malignant identity, calibrated counts, three usable wells per condition, vehicle growth above baseline and the prespecified positive-control response; mechanism results and raw variation remain separate. A treated-count median divided by the vehicle median at or below 0.5 predicts positive, not 50 percent killing. A blinded independent assessor compares the stipulated imaging-volume measurement before treatment and at week six; a decline of at least 20 percent is the invented reference-positive rule, not a clinical response criterion.

anchors.text: The fictional locked rule yields twenty reports and ten no-results among thirty donors. Among reportable cases, six are true positive, three false positive, two false negative and nine true negative, using the exercise's assumed-correct reference labels. There are eight reference positives, twelve negatives, nine positive predictions and eleven negative predictions. Correct classifications are 15/20 (75 percent), sensitivity 6/8 (75 percent), specificity 9/12 (75 percent), and positive predictive value 6/9 (about 66.7 percent). Reportable coverage is 20/30 (about 66.7 percent); 15/30 (50 percent) received a correct reportable classification. The ten no-results keep blank predictions, unknown failure reasons and unspecified outcomes, rather than becoming negative or resistant cases. These truth-based toy metrics do not turn an imperfect real MRI comparator into truth or establish clinical utility.

anchors.text: Preserve the original prediction and version before measuring an independent outcome, compare against the original rule, then investigate agreement, discordance and failures before developing a revision and testing it on new reserved data. A prospective evaluation fixes its predictions before the corresponding outcomes; retrospective analysis examines material and outcomes already observed. Neither label alone establishes useful care. If the toy team changes v1 after inspecting three false positives, v2 is development and v1's matrix and ten no-results remain unchanged. The later breast-study exercise likewise imagines revising a rule after three sensitive dish calls matched intermediate MRI outcomes; those comparisons are not assumed truth labels. Reusing the same twenty cases evaluates fit to the information used for revision. A move from advanced-disease drug A to postoperative drug B changes intended use again, and improvement during several treatments cannot isolate which treatment helped.
